ref: Annex I, Part II, point (1); Art 13(24)
title: Continuous Component Identification & Machine-Readable SBOM
description: Manufacturers shall identify and document vulnerabilities and components contained in products with digital elements, including by drawing up a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) in a commonly used and machine-readable format, covering at the very least top-level dependencies.
applicability: Mandatory (Applies to all products containing third-party or open source software)
stakeholder: DevSecOps Lead, Lead Software Architect, Release Manager
guidance: Integrate automated SBOM generation into CI/CD build pipelines using standard formats (CycloneDX v1.5/1.6 or SPDX v2.3/v3.0). Capture direct and transitive dependencies, package hashes, licenses, and suppliers. Ingest generated SBOMs into Dependency-Track or Black Duck for continuous post-market vulnerability monitoring.
controls: Automated build-time SBOM generators (cdxgen, syft, Black Duck Detect); continuous SBOM management platform (Dependency-Track); SBOM archive repository; automated delta checking between releases.
evidence: Machine-readable SBOM files (CycloneDX JSON / SPDX XML) for every released build; Dependency-Track component inventory; CI/CD SBOM generation build logs.
criteria: Every production release artifact is accompanied by a cryptographically signed, machine-readable SBOM covering 100% of direct dependencies and known transitives; verified by Dependency-Track / Black Duck.
limitations: SonarQube, Coverity, Nessus, and Pentest do not generate or manage machine-readable SBOMs. Black Duck and Nexus IQ generate SBOMs; Dependency-Track provides dedicated ingestion and continuous lifecycle vulnerability analysis.
additional_controls: Centralized SBOM repository; automated signing of SBOMs (Cosign/Sigstore); market surveillance export procedure.
notes: Under Art 13(24), manufacturers must supply the machine-readable SBOM to national market surveillance authorities upon reasoned request without undue delay.

ref: Annex I, Part II, point (2); Art 13(10)
title: Vulnerability Remediation Without Delay via Security Updates
description: In relation to the risks identified, manufacturers shall address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay, including by providing security updates, and where applicable, automatic security updates.
applicability: Mandatory (Binding operational duty across the entire declared support period)
stakeholder: Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT), Sustaining Engineering Lead
guidance: Establish a formalized PSIRT vulnerability remediation SLA: Critical CVEs triaged within 24 hours, patch released within 7-14 calendar days; High CVEs within 30 days. Maintain backporting capability for supported release branches. Deliver patches as modular, standalone security updates.
controls: PSIRT remediation runbook; automated CVE triage alerts; branch maintenance policies for supported versions; fast-track emergency CI/CD release pipeline.
evidence: PSIRT Ticket Tracking Logs; Vulnerability Triage Records; Emergency Patch Release Notes; Time-to-Remediate (MTTR) Compliance Metrics.
criteria: Documented adherence to vulnerability remediation SLAs; 100% of identified exploitable vulnerabilities addressed via patch or verified workaround within SLA windows.
limitations: Tools detect vulnerabilities; they do not write patches, manage engineering sprints, or execute release pipelines. Nexus IQ and Black Duck provide automated PR guidance; Dependency-Track tracks remediation status.
additional_controls: Dedicated PSIRT team; emergency patch release pipeline; contractual SLA monitoring; engineering backport capacity.
notes: Failure to address known exploitable vulnerabilities without delay constitutes a direct violation of Annex I, Part II, incurring fines under Art 64.

title: Regular Security Testing, Verification & Attack Surface Review
description: Manufacturers shall apply effective and regular tests and reviews of the security of the product with digital elements, including during its development and throughout the support period.
applicability: Mandatory (Continuous across development and post-market support phases)
stakeholder: DevSecOps Lead, Security QA Lead, Third-Party Pentest Firm
guidance: Establish a multi-layered verification strategy combining automated continuous testing (SAST, SCA, container scanning) in daily CI/CD with periodic deep dynamic testing (DAST) and annual independent third-party penetration testing. Re-test immediately upon significant architectural changes.
controls: CI/CD automated security testing pipelines; scheduled bi-weekly Nessus/Cyberwatch scans; automated DAST regression suites; annual third-party penetration test engagements.
evidence: Annual Penetration Testing Reports; CI/CD Automated Test Execution Logs; DAST Scan Run Logs; Nessus/Cyberwatch Infrastructure Scan Reports.
criteria: All scheduled scans and tests executed according to calendar; zero unaddressed High/Critical findings past remediation SLA; independent test re-validation sign-off.
limitations: No single tool covers all testing dimensions. Full compliance requires an integrated toolchain combining SAST (Coverity/SonarQube), SCA (Black Duck/Nexus), DAST (Burp/ZAP), and manual Penetration Testing.
additional_controls: Annual third-party security audit budget; automated regression testing suites; DevSecOps pipeline orchestrator.
notes: Testing records must be systematically cataloged and retained as part of the Annex VII technical documentation.

title: Public Disclosure of Remediated Vulnerabilities (Security Advisories)
description: Once a security update has been made available, manufacturers shall publicly disclose information about the fixed vulnerabilities, including a description, information on how to obtain the update, and the severity rating.
applicability: Mandatory (Mandatory for all publicly released security patches; timing must coordinate with update availability)
stakeholder: PSIRT Lead, Technical Communications, Legal / Compliance
guidance: Publish standardized security advisories (Common Security Advisory Framework - CSAF 2.0 JSON and human-readable HTML) on a dedicated security portal. Disclose CVE identifier, CVSS v3.1/v4.0 score and vector, affected product versions, remediated versions, and workarounds for unpatched systems.
controls: CSAF advisory authoring pipeline; public security portal (`security.company.com/advisories`); RSS/email alert distribution feed; CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) coordination.
evidence: Published Security Advisories (HTML and CSAF 2.0 JSON); CVE Registry Records; Customer Advisory Email Broadcast Logs.
criteria: Advisory published synchronously with or immediately following patch availability; CSAF format validates against OASIS schema; accurate CVE and CVSS ratings included.
limitations: Vulnerability scanners do not author, review, or publish legal security advisories or operate CSAF advisory portals. Entirely an organizational PSIRT and communications process.
additional_controls: CSAF 2.0 automation toolchain; CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) partnership or coordination; PSIRT advisory review workflow.
notes: Public disclosure must not precede update availability to prevent weaponization against unpatched users, unless coordinated with CSIRTs.

ref: Annex I, Part II, point (5); Art 13(19)
title: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) Policy
description: Manufacturers shall put in place and enforce a policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure, aligned with international standards such as ISO/IEC 29147 and ISO/IEC 30111.
applicability: Mandatory (Must be publicly accessible and operational before placing product on market)
guidance: Draft, approve, and publish a formal Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Policy aligned with ISO/IEC 29147. Specify scope of in-scope products, safe harbor protections for good-faith security researchers, reporting instructions, PGP communication keys, expected triage response times, and disclosure embargo terms.
controls: Formal CVD policy document approved by CISO and Legal; public web page (`/security/disclosure`); PGP key infrastructure; safe harbor legal commitment.
evidence: Published CVD Policy Document; PGP Public Key in Registry; ISO/IEC 29147 Alignment Matrix; Legal Safe Harbor Clause.
criteria: CVD policy accessible publicly without authentication; clear scope and safe harbor terms; valid PGP key published; response timeline commitments defined.
limitations: Zero automated tool coverage. CVD policy is a governance, legal, and operational framework.
additional_controls: CVD Policy Authoring & Legal Review; alignment with ISO/IEC 29147; integration with Bug Bounty / Researcher platforms (HackerOne/Bugcrowd).
notes: CRA explicitly cites CVD as a key mechanism for collaborative security across the Union.

ref: Annex I, Part II, point (6); Art 13(19)
title: Public External Vulnerability Reporting Contact Point
description: Manufacturers shall facilitate the sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities by providing a contact address for the reporting of vulnerabilities discovered in the product with digital elements.
applicability: Mandatory (Single contact point must be active 24/7/365)
stakeholder: PSIRT Lead, Webmaster, Security Operations Lead
guidance: Deploy RFC 9116 compliant `security.txt` file at `/.well-known/security.txt` and `/security.txt` on all public domains. Maintain a dedicated, monitored email intake inbox (`security@company.com`) backed by an encrypted intake form or bug bounty portal. Provide public PGP encryption keys for secure submissions.
controls: RFC 9116 `security.txt` deployment; dedicated PSIRT ticketing queue; 24/7 inbox monitoring with automated acknowledgment; published PGP encryption key.
evidence: RFC 9116 `security.txt` file URL and content; PSIRT Intake Queue Architecture; First-Response SLA Tracking Logs; Published PGP Public Key.
criteria: `security.txt` validates against RFC 9116 schema; submission to `security@` receives automated acknowledgment within 24 hours; researcher reports routed to PSIRT ticketing.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. This is an operational intake channel and communications endpoint.
additional_controls: RFC 9116 `security.txt` web deployment; PSIRT ticketing system integration (Jira Service Desk / ServiceNow); PGP key rotation procedure.
notes: Contact point must be documented in Annex II Instructions for Use supplied with the product.

title: Cryptographically Secured Update Distribution Infrastructure
description: Manufacturers shall ensure that security updates are distributed securely, including by being cryptographically signed, distributed through authentic channels, and protected against manipulation or downgrade attacks.
applicability: Mandatory (All update release channels, binaries, and firmware distribution servers)
stakeholder: DevSecOps Lead, Release Manager, Infrastructure Security Lead
guidance: Sign all update packages and binaries using cryptographic keys protected inside hardware security modules (HSM) or cloud KMS (Sigstore / Cosign). Enforce signature verification on client devices prior to installation. Distribute updates over TLS-only CDN channels with mutual TLS or strict certificate pinning. Implement anti-rollback / anti-downgrade monotonic version checks.
controls: HSM-backed automated code signing in CI/CD; client-side cryptographic signature verification daemon; TLS 1.3 update repository; monotonic counter anti-rollback enforcement.
evidence: Code Signing Architecture & Key Custody Procedure; Client Signature Verification Code Review / Unit Tests; Anti-Downgrade Test Record; Penetration Test Update Tampering Assessment.
criteria: Client device strictly rejects unsigned, modified, or expired update binaries; downgrade to older vulnerable version is rejected; signing keys secured in HSM with split-custody access.
limitations: Scanners cannot evaluate PKI signing ceremonies or client verification logic. Penetration testing tests client signature verification bypasses and man-in-the-middle tampering.
additional_controls: HSM Key Management infrastructure; update distribution CDN hardening; anti-rollback firmware fuses/counters.
notes: Failure in update security can compromise the entire fleet simultaneously, making this a top priority during conformity assessment.

ref: Annex I, Part II, point (8); Art 13(10)
title: Free-of-Charge Security Updates & Feature Decoupling
description: Manufacturers shall ensure that security updates are made available free of charge throughout the support period, and that security updates are separated from functional updates where technically feasible.
applicability: Mandatory (Default); Conditional (Narrow contractual waiver permitted for bespoke tailor-made B2B software under Recital 64)
stakeholder: Product Manager, Finance Director, Legal Counsel, Software Architect
guidance: Structure commercial software contracts and pricing models to guarantee free security patches for the full duration of the declared support period. Decouple security patches from commercial feature upgrades in Git branches and release artifacts, enabling users to patch without being forced to license new features.
controls: Dual-track release branching strategy (LTS security-only branch vs main feature branch); commercial contract terms template; public update repository with unrestricted access for security patches.
evidence: Release Branching Architecture Spec; Standard Commercial Terms & Conditions (CRA Free Update Guarantee); Multi-Year Software Maintenance Financial Model.
criteria: Security patches compile and deploy independently of paid feature releases; customers can download security patches without subscription renewal or paywall.
limitations: Zero tool coverage. Entirely a commercial, architectural, and contractual obligation.
additional_controls: Software release branching policy; commercial contract review; long-term engineering maintenance funding.
notes: Recital 64 permits custom enterprise software agreements to explicitly negotiate bespoke commercial maintenance terms, provided this is documented in writing.
